title: Verbal periphrases: starting, stopping, repeating, continuing

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know the periphrases *empezar a*, *dejar de* and *volver a* + infinitive, and *seguir* + gerund, from A2 Unit 28. They show a phase of an action: it starts, stops, happens again or continues. They are ideal for telling how a programme began, lost strength or went on.

sections.title: Four periphrases
rows: to begin to: *empezaron a construir casas*
to stop: *el programa dejó de funcionar*
to do again: *volvió a dar más valor a la seguridad*
to keep on: *seguían protegiendo a los grupos ricos*

items.spanish: Algunos países empezaron a construir casas y escuelas con esa ayuda.
items.english: Some countries began to build houses and schools with that aid.

items.spanish: A principios de los años setenta el programa dejó de funcionar.
items.english: In the early 1970s the programme stopped working.

items.spanish: El gobierno de Estados Unidos volvió a dar más valor a la seguridad.
items.english: The US government once again gave more value to security.

items.spanish: Los historiadores siguen discutiendo si el programa fracasó.
items.english: Historians keep on discussing whether the programme failed.

sections.content: The first verb carries the tense and the person (*empezaron*, *dejó*); the second stays in the infinitive, or in the gerund after *seguir*. Use *a* after *empezar* and *volver*, and *de* after *dejar*.
